Calculate Embedded Emissions for Unwrought Aluminium (HS7601)
Enter your input
i EU Emissions Trading System Allowances, the price of a CBAM certificate per tCO2e/t  EU Carbon price (€/tCO₂e)  
**(EUA Cost)**
i Verified carbon intensity (tCO₂e per tonne) of the imported product, as certified by EU-approved verification bodies. (The “embedded emissions” refers to the emissions generated during the production of the imported product in the country where it was made)  Benchmark Emissions (tCO₂e/t)  
**(Embedded Emissions)**
i Benchmark of acceptable CO₂ emissions per tonne for each product type.  ETS benchmark factor (tCO₂e/t) 
i CBAM phase-in rate/factor; an annual adjustment (discount) applied to the benchmark, decreasing each year until 2034 when it reaches 0.  Free allocation (%) 
i Volume of the product imported into the EU.  Imported quantity (tonnes) 
Payable emissions (tCO₂e/t)
Total CBAM Cost (€)
Notes:  
There may be a difference when calculating the price with respect to import volume, carbon price, and benchmark emissions, as the embedded formula may result in minor variations due to decimal rounding. Therefore, the actual value may vary. 
![Alternate Text](https://assets.alcircle.com/web-assets/CBAM_logo.png)
CBAM is applicable to trade volumes starting from 50 metric tonnes. For trade volumes below 50 metric tonnes, CBAM does not apply.
## Usage Procedure – How to use the CBAM Calculator Sheet
  
Enter or update values only in the **INPUT  
PARAMETERS section (Highlighted in blue)** , including   
the carbon price, benchmark emissions, CBAM   
chargeable percentage (as per the phase-in year),  
and imported quantity. 
The system will automatically calculate the **payable  
emissions and the total CBAM cost (€)** based on the   
inputs provided. 
Notes:  
• Change any input value to automatically update CBAM cost.  
• Formula used: Carbon price × payable emissions × quantity.  
• Model aligned with CBAM supplier-side illustrative methodology.

Ardakan Industrial Ceramics Co. manufactures alumina-based industrial ceramics and silicate-based industrial ceramics. It offers alumina grinding balls and liners for tiles and ceramics, porcelain, glazing, pigment, cement, and pulverization industries; alumina-silicate based ceramic balls for use in oil, natural gas, petrochemical, and chemical industries as a neutralize bed and support of catalyst in towers, vessels, and reactors; wear resistance high alumina liners for steel, iron, and mining industries. The company was founded in 1995 and is based in Isfahan, Iran
